title: Postpartum Hemorrhage — Staged Response
sources: California Maternal Quality Care Collaborative (CMQCC) OB Hemorrhage Toolkit — staged obstetric hemorrhage care guidelines.
ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage. Obstet Gynecol. 2017;130(4):e168-e186.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap. Built on the CMQCC staged obstetric hemorrhage framework (Stage 0-3), which drives blood-bank/OR escalation in most US labor & delivery units. A classification, not a point score, so uses the calculator engine's classification type rather than additive.

purpose: Stages ongoing postpartum bleeding by cumulative estimated blood loss and vital-sign trend to drive escalation — from active management through massive transfusion activation.

tiers.label: Stage 0 — normal
tiers.description: Estimated blood loss < 500 mL after vaginal delivery (< 1000 mL after cesarean), normal vital signs.
tiers.mortality: Active management of the third stage (uterotonic, uterine massage, cord traction); continue routine post-delivery monitoring.

tiers.label: Stage 1
tiers.description: EBL 500-999 mL after vaginal delivery (or trending toward 1000+ mL after cesarean), OR any abnormal vital signs with ongoing bleeding above the expected amount.
tiers.mortality: First-line uterotonics (oxytocin, methylergonovine, or carboprost per contraindications), IV access ×2, type & screen, quantify blood loss, increase monitoring frequency, activate the OB hemorrhage team.

tiers.label: Stage 2
tiers.description: Continued bleeding with cumulative EBL up to ~1500 mL despite first-line measures.
tiers.mortality: Second-line uterotonics, tranexamic acid, order blood products (type & crossmatch, have PRBCs available), move toward the OR for exam under anesthesia / uterine tamponade / surgical management, consider bimanual uterine compression while preparing.

tiers.label: Stage 3 — massive hemorrhage
tiers.description: EBL > 1500 mL, OR more than 2 units PRBC transfused, OR unstable vital signs, OR clinical suspicion of DIC/coagulopathy.
tiers.mortality: Activate massive transfusion protocol, move to definitive surgical management (uterine artery ligation, B-Lynch compression suture, or hysterectomy as a last resort), involve interventional radiology / anesthesia / ICU early, treat coagulopathy with lab-guided products.

interpretation.label: Cumulative estimated blood loss, not a single reading, drives the stage
interpretation.detail: Quantitative blood loss (weighing pads/drapes) is more accurate than visual estimation, which systematically underestimates — use it whenever available. Re-stage continuously; a patient can move through several stages in minutes.

buildNote: classification engine, matching the killip-classification pattern — a staged framework, not a point-summed score. Cross-references postpartum-hemorrhage (the existing management reference) and hemorrhagic-shock-mtp via aliases/keywords since calculators don't carry a `related` field.
